elements.element: Preferred: no non-compete or field-of-use restriction is imposed on Customer (Ono)
elements.evidence: "neither Ono or its Affiliates ... shall Commercialize in the Ono Territory: (i) a product that includes ... (each a 'Competing Product')"

elements.element: Preferred: no post-termination field-of-use tail on Customer
elements.evidence: "neither Ono nor its Affiliates shall Commercialize a Competing Product ... prior to the twelve (12) month anniversary of the date such termination takes effect"

elements.element: Fallback: restriction limited to a named/defined competing product
elements.evidence: "an agent that is a [ * ] (other than Binimetinib) ... (each a \"Competing Product\")" — restriction is scoped to the defined Competing Product only

elements.element: Fallback: restriction operates during the term (no open-ended post-term restraint)
elements.evidence: in-term restraint "Prior to the [ * ]" plus a now-bounded tail "prior to the twelve (12) month anniversary of the date such termination takes effect"; official check "no open-ended compete restriction on Customer remains" ok
"prior to the twelve (12) month anniversary of the date such termination takes effect" (replacing the redacted "[ * ] anniversary")
"(A) conducting internal research, development or manufacturing activities with respect to any compound or product"
"(B) Commercializing any Competing Product acquired by Ono or its Affiliates in connection with a merger with, or an acquisition of, a Third Party or of the business or assets of a Third Party"

offending_extra_words: with respect to any compound or product
nothing in this Section 8.2 shall restrict Ono or its Affiliates from
reasons: Fallback is complete on its material terms: the post-termination tail is capped at twelve (12) months, the restraint remains limited to the defined 'Competing Product', and both required carve-outs (internal development; M&A-acquired products) are added operatively.
Preferred is not met and could not be, since a reciprocal in-term exclusivity plus a capped post-term tail on Customer survives.

Minimality fails: the single operation expands 14 words to 81 (ratio 5.79) and changes 86.8% of the anchored span, breaching the official gates. The 12-month cap alone needed only a numeral substitution; the carve-outs should have been a separate, tighter insertion anchored on unchanged text.

Unnecessary boilerplate and over-broad wording inflate the edit: 'Notwithstanding anything to the contrary,' is superfluous, and 'internal research, development or manufacturing activities with respect to any compound or product' reaches beyond the playbook's 'internal development' carve-out (manufacturing; any compound or product).

Intent is preserved: the reciprocal in-term exclusivity, Array's termination right, and the royalty-period termination mechanic are untouched, and 'Third Party' is a defined term, so no dangling mechanic or undefined term is introduced.
